questions.statement: Choose the correct article: 'She works as ____ engineer in a public company.'

options.text: a
options.feedback: 'A' is used before consonants, not before the vowel sound of 'engineer'.

options.text: the
options.feedback: 'The' would imply a specific engineer already mentioned.

options.text: no article
options.feedback: A countable singular profession requires a determiner.

options.text: an
options.feedback: 'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article is 'an'.

questions.explanation:
Las professions se introducen con articulo indefinido 'a' cuando se habla en general.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'Mountains are ____ important source of clean water.'

options.text: an
options.feedback: 'An important source' agrees with the singular predicate noun 'source'.

options.text: a source
options.feedback: The indefinite article is required before the singular vowel-initial noun.

options.text: many important
options.feedback: 'Many' cannot modify a singular noun such as 'source'.

options.text: no article
options.feedback: The singular predicate noun requires the determiner 'an'.

questions.explanation:
El sujeto es plural pero el predicado es singular, por eso el articulo corresponde a 'source'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses 'the' correctly?

options.text: The sun rises in the east.
options.feedback: 'The sun' is unique for all speakers, so the definite article is required.

options.text: A sun rises in the east.
options.feedback: 'A sun' would suggest one among many, which is incorrect here.

options.text: Sun rises in the east.
options.feedback: A count noun needs an article even in a general statement.

options.text: The a sun rises in the east.
options.feedback: Two articles cannot be combined in a noun phrase.

questions.explanation:
'The sun' es un referente unico y conocido, por lo que exige articulo definido. Es una de las estructuras mas frecuentes en el examen.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the difference between 'a glass of water' and 'the glass of water'?

options.text: Both articles mean exactly the same thing here
options.feedback: The two articles carry different definiteness values.

options.text: 'The' is only used with plural nouns
options.feedback: 'The' is used with both singular and plural nouns.

options.text: 'A' can only appear before uncountable nouns
options.feedback: 'A' appears before countable singular nouns such as 'glass'.

options.text: 'A' introduces something not yet identified; 'the' points to a known one
options.feedback: The choice of article depends on whether the referent is known.

questions.explanation:
'A glass' introduce un objeto no identificado; 'the glass' se refiere a uno ya conocido o determinado.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'I would like ____ apple and some bread, please.'
questions.context: Articulos con contables e incontables, Guayaquil.

options.text: a
options.feedback: 'A' is not used before a vowel sound.

options.text: an
options.feedback: 'An apple' is the correct singular count form, contrasting with 'some bread'.

options.text: some
options.feedback: 'Some' cannot modify the countable singular 'apple'.

options.text: many
options.feedback: 'Many' requires a plural count noun.

questions.explanation:
'Apple' es contable singular y empieza por vocal, de modo que lleva 'an'; 'bread' ya lleva 'some'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the zero article correctly?

options.text: She studies the mathematics at the university.
options.feedback: 'The mathematics' would refer to a specific field or a textbook.

options.text: She studies a mathematics at the university.
options.feedback: 'A' cannot be used with an uncountable subject name.

options.text: She studies of mathematics at the university.
options.feedback: The preposition 'of' is not part of this construction.

options.text: She studies mathematics at the university.
options.feedback: 'Mathematics' as a subject takes the zero article in this general sense.

questions.explanation:
Los nombres de disciplinas se usan sin articulo cuando se consideran en general. Conviene memorizar esta combinacion como una sola unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'He is ____ best player of the team.' Choose the correct article.

options.text: a
options.feedback: 'A' cannot introduce a superlative comparison.

options.text: an
options.feedback: 'An' cannot introduce a superlative comparison.

options.text: the
options.feedback: Superlative adjectives require the definite article 'the'.

options.text: no article
options.feedback: The definite article is obligatory before a superlative.

questions.explanation:
El superlativo lleva siempre articulo definido: 'the best player'. Este matiz se comprueba comparando con el resto de opciones.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence with the correct use of the articles.
questions.context: Evaluacion del uso de articulos, Guayaquil.

options.text: He waited for hour and a half at airport.
options.feedback: Both articles are missing from the countable nouns.

options.text: He waited for an hour and a half at the airport.
options.feedback: 'An hour and a half' and 'the airport' both take the correct articles.

options.text: He waited for a hour and half at the airport.
options.feedback: 'Half' as a noun also requires a determiner: 'a half'.

options.text: He waited for an hour and a half at a airport.
options.feedback: 'The airport' is specific here, so the indefinite article is wrong.

questions.explanation:
Cada sustantivo contable singular lleva el articulo que le corresponde segun el contexto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why does the noun 'the' appear before 'the Equator'?

options.text: It identifies a single unique feature on the planet
options.feedback: The Equator is one unique line, so the definite article is required.

options.text: It indicates that the Equator is plural
options.feedback: The article does not change the number of the name.

options.text: It shows that the Equator belongs to a country
options.feedback: The Equator crosses several countries and is not owned by any of them.

options.text: It replaces the preposition 'on'
options.feedback: The article is a determiner and does not replace prepositions.

questions.explanation:
Los nombres geograficos que designan un unico objeto del planeta llevan articulo definido.

questions.statement: Complete: 'Water is ____ of the most important natural resources.'

options.text: a
options.feedback: 'A of the' is not a valid construction in English.

options.text: an
options.feedback: 'An of the' is grammatically impossible.

options.text: many
options.feedback: 'Many' is used with plural count nouns and not before 'of the'.

options.text: one
options.feedback: 'One of the most important' is the standard superlative construction.

questions.explanation:
La estructura correcta de comparacion superlativa es 'one of the most' mas el sustantivo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the function of the article in 'She is playing the piano'?

options.text: It marks the activity as a unique skill or function
options.feedback: 'The piano' in this idiomatic use refers to the activity of playing.

options.text: It refers to a specific piano owned by the speaker
options.feedback: The idiomatic meaning is the activity, not a particular instrument.

options.text: It indicates plurality
options.feedback: The article has no plural function here.

options.text: It replaces the verb 'playing'
options.feedback: An article cannot replace the main verb of the sentence.

questions.explanation:
Aqui el articulo definido se usa porque el sustantivo designa una actividad o una ability unica en el contexto.

questions.statement: Which sentence uses articles incorrectly?

options.text: She borrowed a library book.
options.feedback: 'A library book' is correct before the consonant sound.

options.text: She borrowed an library book.
options.feedback: A consonant sound requires 'a', never 'an'.

options.text: She borrowed the library book.
options.feedback: 'The' is possible if the book was already identified.

options.text: She borrowed some library books.
options.feedback: 'Some' with a plural countable noun is correct.

questions.explanation:
'An' no puede usarse delante de un sonido consonante como el de 'library'. Es una de las estructuras mas frecuentes en el examen.

questions.statement: Complete the question: '____ is the capital of Ecuador?'

options.text: Which
options.feedback: 'Which' selects among a limited set already named.

options.text: Whose
options.feedback: 'Whose' asks about possession.

options.text: Where
options.feedback: 'Where' asks about a place rather than a name.

options.text: What
options.feedback: 'What is the capital of Ecuador?' is the standard neutral question.

questions.explanation:
La pregunta se refiere a un objeto unico y conocido, por eso corresponde 'What' con 'the'.

questions.statement: Read the text: 'An old man lives next door. The man never sleeps.' What does the second 'the' do?

options.text: It refers to a different old man
options.feedback: The text presents only one old man in the neighbourhood.

options.text: It marks the sentence as a question
options.feedback: The article has no interrogative function.

options.text: It refers back to the old man already mentioned
options.feedback: The definite article signals a known referent in the second mention.

options.text: It indicates that the man is unique in the world
options.feedback: The article marks knownness, not global uniqueness.

questions.explanation:
La segunda mencion vuelve a un referente ya presentado, por eso requiere el articulo definido.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses 'a' correctly?

options.text: A cars broke down on the highway.
options.feedback: The indefinite article cannot be placed before a plural noun.

options.text: The car break down on the highway.
options.feedback: That combines the definite article with an incorrect verb form.

options.text: A car broke down on the highway.
options.feedback: 'A car' introduces one unspecified car, which is the correct use.

options.text: A of car broke down on the highway.
options.feedback: The preposition 'of' does not belong in this phrase.

questions.explanation:
El articulo indefinido precede a un sustantivo contable singular no identificado. Conviene memorizar esta combinacion como una sola unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is wrong with the sentence 'She has the beautiful brown eyes'?
questions.context: Revision de pronombres y articulos, Quito.

options.text: Nothing is wrong with the sentence
options.feedback: Placing a determiner between adjectives is not standard English.

options.text: The articles should not separate the adjectives from the noun
options.feedback: English places the determiners before the whole adjective+noun phrase.

options.text: 'Beautiful' should be a noun
options.feedback: 'Beautiful' is an adjective and belongs in the adjective chain.

options.text: 'Eyes' should be singular
options.feedback: The plural is required because the possessive indicates more than one.

questions.explanation:
En ingles los adjetivos atributivos se colocación antes del sustantivo: no se usa 'the' entre ellos.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly uses 'of' after a noun?

options.text: She drank a cup tea.
options.feedback: The preposition 'of' is missing in this construction.

options.text: She drank a of cup tea.
options.feedback: The order of the nouns around 'of' is reversed.

options.text: She drank a cup of tea.
options.feedback: 'A cup of tea' follows the standard noun-plus-'of' pattern.

options.text: She drank the cup of the tea.
options.feedback: That adds a definite article that is not part of the standard phrase.

questions.explanation:
'A cup of tea' es la construccion estandar con 'of' entre dos sustantivos. Este matiz se comprueba comparando con el resto de opciones.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that uses articles consistently throughout.

options.text: He is mechanic and works in garage on some weekends.
options.feedback: The countable nouns 'mechanic' and 'garage' lack their articles.

options.text: He is a mechanic and works in the garage on some weekends.
options.feedback: Each determiner matches the countability and definiteness of its noun.

options.text: He is the mechanic and works in a garage on some weekends.
options.feedback: 'The mechanic' would imply a mechanic already mentioned.

options.text: He is a mechanic and works in an garage on some weekends.
options.feedback: 'An' cannot be used before the consonant sound of 'garage'.

questions.explanation:
La oracion correcta aplica 'a' a la profession, 'the' a las lugares ya identificados y 'some' al sustantivo incontable.

options.text: bed

options.text: the bed
options.feedback: 'The bed' would refer to a specific bed already mentioned.

options.text: a bed

options.text: my bed

En las expresiones fijas del uso cotidiano, 'bed' aparece sin articulo. Es una de las estructuras mas frecuentes en el examen.

questions.statement: Read the sentence: 'The students in the first group finished earlier than the ones in the second.' What does 'the ones' refer to?

options.text: The students in the first group
options.feedback: The first group is named explicitly and does not need a substitute.

options.text: The teacher of the second group
options.feedback: No teacher is mentioned in the sentence.

options.text: The students in the second group
options.feedback: 'The ones' stands for 'the students' with the second group's modifier.

options.text: The lessons of the second group
options.feedback: Only students, not lessons, are referred to as plural entities here.

'The ones' sustituye a un sustantivo ya mencionado y por eso lleva el articulo definido.
